records.name: Greymanes
records.summary: Kliff's mercenary company and the protectors of Pailune, all but destroyed in the opening attack.
records.body: The company was built to keep Pailune's roads and towns safe; after Jian's death [[character:kliff]] holds the banner from the rebuilt camp on [[place:howling-hill]]. Survivors are found one by one through the main story. Greymane commissions are short repeatable tasks that pay a flat reward and refresh daily. New comrades arrive through the Grounds of the Sunrise work, and they grow stronger when the camp is upgraded rather than by earning their own experience.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Helping the company rebuild, finishing its story beats, and taking camps back from occupiers raise standing fastest. Alliance opens allied troops on Greymane ground, shops that sell only to friends, and gathering spots the company otherwise keeps closed.

sources.title: Game8: How to Level Up Comrades

records.name: Black Bears
records.summary: Myurdin's hostile mercenary company, responsible for the attack on the Greymane camp.
records.body: [[character:myurdin]] leads a conquest company that smashed the Greymanes on the opening night and now sits on [[place:pailune]]. They want Pailune under their rule, not a peacekeeping charter. Kliff meets them in the prologue raid and again when the company pushes north to take the city back. Story fights against Myurdin and his occupation troops are how this banner shows up; it is not a joinable house.

records.name: House Celeste
records.summary: Ducal house of Hernand, descended from the knight Canta, seated at Hernand Castle.
records.body: [[character:charles-celeste]] holds the duchy from [[place:hernand-castle]], and the line traces itself to the knight Canta. The house wants Hernand stable while lesser houses handle workshops, maps and coin. Kliff deals with Celeste officials once he reaches the city and starts taking work from the court. It is a core banner on the faction lists, not a camp you assault.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Court errands, city commissions and freeing Hernand camps raise standing. Alliance brings allied troops in Celeste land, exclusive vendors and gathering spots the duchy otherwise keeps shut.

records.name: House Serkis
records.summary: Marquis house that runs Hernand's internal affairs as Celeste's right hand.
records.body: [[character:marquis-serkis]] (Alan Serkis) keeps the duchy's books and streets in order from Oakenshield Manor at [[place:serkis-estate]], working as House Celeste's right hand. The house wants Hernand's daily business to run without the duke having to watch every ledger. Kliff is set to rebuild work after Golden Greed, including the first camp jobs that start at the Serkis seat. [[quest:first-step-to-rebuilding]] is the early beat that puts the marquis on the page.

reputation.notes: Standing runs War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. City administration jobs and the early rebuild chain move this house. Alliance unlocks allied troops, exclusive vendors and restricted nodes on Serkis ground.

records.name: House Grace
records.summary: Count's house in southern Hernand, known for workshops and technical support.
records.body: [[character:alistair-grace]] governs from the Reedfield Graves country in southern Hernand. The house backs regional rule with workshop and machine work rather than a border army. Kliff crosses their ground while tracking the reed-field trouble around [[place:reedfield-graves]]. Guides list it as a core Hernand house, not a hostile camp.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Southern Hernand jobs and workshop errands raise standing. Alliance opens allied troops, exclusive vendors and gathering spots the count otherwise keeps closed.

records.name: House Lanford
records.summary: Marquis house that holds Calphade, the militarized Hernand–Pailune frontier.
records.body: [[character:stefan-lanford]] keeps the Calphade march from [[place:calphade-castle]] and is called the Unyielding Shield. The house wants the Hernand–Pailune border held, not opened to Black Bear traffic. Kliff fights through Chapter 6 beside Lanford troops, including the push that ends with [[character:cassius-morten]]. Stefan is named as a long-time friend of Jian and close to the Greymanes; that friendship is taken from a search snippet, not a page fetched in full.

reputation.notes: Standing runs War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. The Calphade chapter, frontier commissions and taking back occupied posts raise this house. Alliance unlocks allied troops on the march, exclusive vendors and restricted nodes.

records.name: House Roberts
records.summary: Wealthy merchant-noble house in Hernand, known for hosting events.
records.body: [[character:leon-roberts]] heads a count's line that made its name in trade rather than a border command. The house wants wealth and guests; it hosts gatherings rather than mustering a march. Kliff meets Roberts people around [[place:frowde-camp]] and Bluemont Manor country, which the lists name together as their seat. Guides treat it as a lesser Hernand house, not a story antagonist.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Trade errands and guest-house jobs raise standing. Alliance opens allied troops, exclusive vendors and gathering spots the family otherwise keeps for itself.

records.name: House Felix
records.summary: Lesser Hernand house known for mapmaking and an intellectual movement.
records.body: House Felix sits among Hernand's lesser noble lines and is named for charts and a learned circle rather than a field army. It wants maps and ideas in circulation, not a seat on the ducal council. Kliff does not get a dedicated Felix chapter; the house appears on the faction roster as background court texture. No source read here names a living head, so leadership is left blank rather than guessed.

reputation.notes: Standing uses War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Small Hernand jobs tied to scholars and survey work are the likely climb. Alliance would open allied troops, exclusive vendors and restricted nodes if the house tracks that far.

records.name: House Alfonso
records.summary: Lesser Hernand house of spearmasters that keeps a family combat manual.
records.body: House Alfonso is a lesser noble line in Hernand that treats the spear as family craft. It wants that manual preserved and stages martial contests to keep the style alive. Kliff can run into their tournaments as side work rather than a main-story siege. No source read here names a current head, so the leader field is omitted.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Contest work and spear-school errands raise standing. Alliance unlocks allied troops, exclusive vendors and gathering spots the house otherwise keeps closed.

records.name: Scholastone Institute
records.summary: Hernand academy founded by troll scholars, open to every race, that studies the Abyss.
records.body: [[character:grundir]] is dean of the school at [[place:scholastone-institute]], a house of study started by troll scholars and kept open to every race. The institute wants Abyss research on the record, which puts it at odds with more traditional troll villages. Kliff is sent there in Chapter 4 for letters, rifts and [[character:octavius]]'s experiments. [[quest:scholastone]] and the jobs around it are the first long visit.

reputation.notes: Ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Chapter 4 school work and later scholarly requests raise standing. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted study sites and allied help on institute ground.

records.name: Goldleaf Merchant Guild
records.summary: Pywel's largest merchant guild, goblin-run and profit-first, based in Hernand.
records.body: [[character:kailok]] sits at the top of the guild while [[character:shakatu]] runs the day-to-day trade from [[place:goldleaf-merchant-guild]]. Goldleaf wants profit across Pywel, not a moral charter; the Silvermoon collective is later written as its foil. Kliff investigates the guildhouse in Chapter 2 and can walk out with Shakatu as a trade ally after the uprising there. [[quest:the-dark-veil]] and [[quest:rebellion-of-revolution]] are the story beats that put the ledgers on the table.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Trade jobs, the Chapter 2 guild investigation and later merchant work raise standing. Alliance unlocks exclusive vendors, restricted resource nodes and allied help at Goldleaf posts.

records.name: Vellua Fishermen's Guild
records.summary: Coastal fishing and trade guild at Vellua, repeatedly hit by pirates.
records.body: The guild works the southern Hernand shore from [[place:vellua]], selling catch and running coastal trade. It wants boats on the water and pirates off it; the Dancing Catfish crews keep testing that. Kliff meets the village as a fishing port rather than a court. No source read here names a guildmaster, so leadership is omitted.

reputation.notes: Standing runs War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Shore commissions, pirate bounties and village requests raise this guild. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted coastal nodes and allied help around Vellua.

records.name: Pororin Forest Guardians
records.summary: Isolated sanctuary community in Pororin Forest, unfriendly to outsiders.
records.body: The guardians keep a hidden village at [[place:pororin]] and treat the forest as a closed sanctuary. They want strangers out, not a seat in Hernand's court. Kliff reaches them only after entering the woods; they are listed as a community, not a bandit camp you clear on sight. No source read here names a chief, so the leader field is left empty.

records.name: Kharonso Troll Alliance
records.summary: Traditional troll village alliance in southwest Hernand, at odds with Scholastone.
records.body: The alliance is a conservative troll community in a hidden mountain village in southwest Hernand. It wants old custom kept, and it clashes with [[faction:scholastone-institute]]'s open, modernising school. Kliff can meet the village as a community, not an on-sight raid. Headquarters is omitted because no Kharonso place record exists yet.

records.name: Beggars' Alliance
records.summary: Mutual-aid network of vagrants and refugees in Hernand.
records.body: The alliance is a street-level compact among vagrants and refugees in Hernand, not a noble house. It wants its people fed and left alone, not a charter on the castle wall. Kliff can pick up small requests from beggars in the city; [[quest:mysterious-man]] starts with a coin asked in Hernand, which sits in that world even if the giver is not named as a guild officer. No source read here names a leader.

records.name: Hornsplitter's Guards
records.summary: Kailok's personal elite force, fought as the Chapter 2 guild uprising bosses.
records.body: [[character:kailok]] keeps this armed retinue as private security while also heading the non-hostile [[faction:goldleaf-merchant-guild]]. The guards exist to protect his person and his ledgers, not to keep Hernand's peace. Kliff fights them at the close of Chapter 2 when the guildhouse revolt comes to a head. [[quest:rebellion-of-revolution]] is the Shakatu talk that starts that chain; [[quest:cheers-echoing-from-the-edge]] is the Chapter 2 boss fight.

records.name: St. Halssius's House of Healing
records.summary: Hernand asylum that confines the politically inconvenient under a medical name.
records.body: [[character:augustine]] heads the house at [[place:house-of-healing]]. On paper it treats troubled minds; in practice it locks away people the city wants gone. Kliff is walked through the building during Familiar Curses and finds a prison, not a ward. [[quest:familiar-curses]] is the story visit; the faction lists mark the house hostile.

records.name: Fundamentalist Goblins
records.summary: Hernand band that claims scholarly purpose while operating like common thieves.
records.body: This goblin band talks like a school and works like a theft ring. It wants loot dressed up as study, not a chair at Scholastone. Kliff meets them as hostile field enemies in Hernand rather than as a joinable college. No source read here names a leader.

records.name: Bleed Bandits
records.summary: Hernand crime ring that traffics Dreamer's Bliss and takes slaves.
records.body: The Bleed Bandits are an organised crime crew in Hernand, not a fallen house. They push a drug called Dreamer's Bliss and take people as property. Kliff meets them as hostile camps and bounties, not as a court faction. No source read here names a boss of the ring.

records.name: Wolf Trackers
records.summary: Pywel-wide hunting band that chases legendary quarry for sport.
records.body: The Wolf Trackers roam beyond one duchy and hunt famous beasts for the chase, not for a town's larder. They want trophies, not a charter. Kliff meets them as hostile hunters in the field. The Hernand faction table is where the lists park them; no source read here names a captain.

records.name: Southern Bandits
records.summary: Lesser-known robbery crew operating in southern Hernand.
records.body: The Southern Bandits are a small pillage crew on Hernand's south side, not a named house. They want road loot and abandoned farms. Kliff meets them as ordinary hostile camps rather than a chapter boss. No source read here names a leader.

records.name: Reed Devil
records.summary: Demon-led scarecrow host haunting Sunset Valley and the Reed Fields.
records.body: The Reed Devil is both the name of a demon and the banner over the spirits that wear scarecrow bodies in its fields. It wants that country feared and empty of ordinary travel. Kliff tracks the trouble around [[place:reedfield-graves]] in Chapter 3. [[quest:dance-with-the-devil]] is the story beat that puts the host on the map; no personal name beyond Reed Devil appears in the sources read here.

records.name: Cassius Morten
records.summary: Loyalist band listed under Cassius Morten's own name after he betrays Calphade.
records.body: Game8 files this military remnant under the name Cassius Morten rather than a house title; it is the loyalist band that stayed with the fallen Calphade commander after he turned on the marquis. They want his banner held at [[place:calphade-castle]], not Lanford's. Kliff meets them as the Chapter 6 castle opposition. [[quest:traitor-ch6]] is the fight that ends the chain; a search snippet on gaming.tools files the same group as faction_silvermorten.

records.name: Dancing Catfish Pirates
records.summary: Coastal pirate crew whose followers treat Sir Catfish with near-fanatical loyalty.
records.body: These pirates work Hernand's coast and prey on fishing traffic, including the Vellua boats. They want plunder, and the crews treat Sir Catfish as more than a captain. Kliff meets them as hostile shore fights. The row is Game8-only in the research file; Sir Catfish has no character record in this pass, so leadership is omitted rather than invented.

records.name: Crow Brothers
records.summary: Mobile sorcerous killers who serve Hexe Marie and hunt her favour.
records.body: [[character:draven]], adopted by [[character:hexe-marie]], leads this slaughter band across Pailune and Demeniss. They want the witch's affection and the souls she points them at, not a town to govern. Kliff meets them in the Chapter 5 hunt that starts with the Axiom Archive raid and the taking of White Crow. [[quest:black-and-white]] and [[quest:crowcaller]] are the story beats that put Draven on the road.

records.name: Mistwood Hunters
records.summary: Poachers in the Wayward Woods who hunt woodland spirits for profit.
records.body: The Mistwood Hunters work the Wayward Woods and treat forest spirits as stock. They want coin from those kills, not a village charter. Kliff meets them as hostile woods enemies in Pailune country. The row is Game8-only in the research file, and no leader is named.

records.name: Church of Solumen
records.summary: Southern Pywel church of the light god Solumen, wary of prayers for miracles.
records.body: The church worships Solumen and is written as the largest light faith in southern Pywel. It wants reverence without miracle-begging; asking the god to intervene is treated as taboo. Kliff meets parish buildings and clergy as civilian institutions, not as a raid target. The row is Game8-only in the research file, so the wide southern claim is assumed from that single list.

records.name: Hernandian Parish of Solumen
records.summary: Hernand branch of Solumen worship, run apart from the central cathedral.
records.body: This parish is the Hernand office of Solumen worship and is written as independent from the central cathedral. It wants local rites kept under local priests. Kliff visits [[place:hernand-church]] in Chapter 5 for a relic and the Pillar of Radiance. The row is Game8-only in the research file; tying the parish seat to that church is assumed from the city church being the named Solumen building.

records.name: Antumbra Order
records.summary: Scattered dark-worship order that uses sacrifice and calls evil a path to equality.
records.body: The Antumbra Order is a hostile faith spread across Pywel rather than pinned to one castle. It wants light and ordinary life profaned, and it sells that as a kind of equality. Kliff meets its people as enemies, not as a parish he can join. The row is Game8-only in the research file, and no leader is named.

records.name: Jijeong School
records.summary: Secret Eastern spiritual and martial discipline based at Jijeong Temple.
records.body: The school keeps a closed Eastern discipline of spirit and martial work at [[place:jijeong-temple]]. It wants students tested on its own terms, not advertised in Hernand. Kliff reaches the temple during Chapter 9 when the grounds are in uproar. [[quest:jijeong-temple-in-chaos]] and the disciple path that follows are the story visit; the Chief Monk is named in Game8 only and has no character record in this pass, so leadership is omitted.

records.name: Order of Light
records.summary: Knightly order Matthias founded after his lord fell, met as an honour duel in Hernand.
records.body: [[character:matthias]] raised this order from fellow wanderers after the lord he served was gone. They want a test of arms, not a city to occupy; the first meeting is an honour duel in Hernand's square during [[quest:for-honor]]. The house is not marked hostile-on-sight on the faction lists, even though that duel is a story boss. Headquarters is the city square at [[place:hernand-castle]] because that is where the order first appears; they are otherwise written as wandering.

records.name: Lonely Jackals
records.summary: Former Greymane allies who now occupy Pailune under Ludvig with the Black Bears.
records.body: [[character:ludvig]] turned the Jackals into Black Bear collaborators after Jian's death and now leans on the people of [[place:pailune]]. They want the city held for the occupation, not the old Greymane peace charter. Kliff meets them as the Chapter 7 castle opposition and hunts Ludvig through more than one boss form. [[quest:lonely-jackals]] is the named fight; Jackals is only the short form of the same banner.

records.name: Pailune Militia
records.summary: Regional defense force around Pailune's capital, resisting the occupation.
records.body: The militia is the home defense of the Pailune capital country, not a mercenary charter. It wants the Black Bear and Jackal occupation off the city. Kliff fights beside or through their ground during the Homecoming push. [[quest:shadows-over-pailune]] and [[quest:healing-pailune]] sit on that stretch; no source read here names a militia captain.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Liberating the capital and finishing Homecoming work raise standing. Alliance opens allied troops in the city, exclusive vendors and restricted nodes.

records.name: Blue Fangs
records.summary: Beighen resistance led by Torstein, hiding among villagers as the Beighen Militia.
records.body: [[character:torstein]], once vice-captain of Jian's guard, runs this resistance from [[place:beighen]]. They want the occupation bled out of southeast Pailune while looking like ordinary villagers. Kliff is pointed at the Blue Fangs during [[quest:bared-fang]] and works with Torstein again when the company comes home. Beighen Militia is the same banner under its village name.

reputation.notes: Standing runs War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Homecoming jobs around Beighen raise this militia. Alliance unlocks allied troops in the village, exclusive vendors and restricted nodes.

records.name: Beighen Tribe
records.summary: Mountain-isolated tribe at Beighen that keeps ancestral-spirit worship.
records.body: The Beighen Tribe lives at [[place:beighen]] in southeast Pailune, cut off by mountains and still keeping ancestral-spirit rites. It wants that isolation and those rites left alone. Kliff meets the villagers as the same settlement that hides the [[faction:blue-fangs]]. No source read here names a tribal chief separate from Torstein's militia role, so leadership is omitted.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Village requests in Beighen raise standing. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted mountain nodes and allied help among the tribe.

records.name: Knytlingar
records.summary: Weakened northern Pailune clan that can no longer hold invaders off.
records.body: [[character:olvald]] is chief of this northern Pailune clan. They want their ground kept, but the lists say they can no longer push invaders back. Kliff meets them as a tribal community rather than a raid target. Headquarters is omitted because no named Knytlingar village record exists yet.

records.name: Longleaf
records.summary: Tree-dwelling Wayward Woods tribe that uses sacred lanterns and shuns outsiders.
records.body: The Longleaf keep to the trees in the Wayward Woods and light sacred lanterns as part of that life. They want outsiders out of the canopy. Kliff meets them as a closed woodland people, not as a bandit camp. No source read here names a chief, and no Longleaf village record exists, so leadership and headquarters are omitted.

records.name: Skoghorn
records.summary: Western Pailune mountain tribe that worships mountain spirits.
records.body: The Skoghorn hold the western Pailune mountains from [[place:skoghorn]] and keep mountain-spirit rites. A fandom snippet says they once practiced child sacrifice; that past is single-source and is treated as assumed here. Kliff meets the village as a tribal community, not an on-sight raid. No source read here names a living chief.

records.name: Stjar
records.summary: Northern Pailune clan split between ancestor rites at Totemfelt and weather worship at Skallcove.
records.body: The Stjar keep two northern villages: ancestor worship at [[place:totemfelt]] and weather-deity worship at Skallcove. They want both rites kept, even though the clan is split. Kliff meets them as tribal communities rather than a single castle faction. Skallcove has no place record yet, so the named headquarters is Totemfelt.

records.name: Odeck
records.summary: Old far-northern Pailune tribe that now lives by logging, once famed for a defending general.
records.body: The Odeck are written as one of Pailune's oldest tribes, now living by the axe at [[place:odeck]] in the Kweiden country. They want that logging life, and they still remember a heroic general who once held Pailune. Kliff can take a two-part faction chain named Executioner of Justice and Slumbering Soul; those titles have no quest records here yet. A hidden merchant is said to unlock Odeck-tribe weapons after that work; both details come from search snippets.

reputation.notes: Ranks run War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. The Odeck faction chain and village jobs raise standing. Alliance unlocks exclusive vendors, restricted logging nodes and allied help in the north.

records.name: House Thorel
records.summary: Traditional royal house of Demeniss, powerless while King Edward lies comatose.
records.body: [[character:edward-thorel]] is still the named king, but he is comatose and named no heir, so the house holds the title without the court. They want the old royal line restored; Caliburn and Bastier's blocs hold the real knives. Kliff and Damiane's Demeniss work circles that vacancy. The Demeniss Bound title is named in research and has no quest record here yet; [[quest:to-demeniss]] is the story beat that puts the company on that road.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Demeniss story work that sides with the old crown raises standing. Alliance would open exclusive vendors, restricted palace rooms and allied help among Thorel loyalists.

records.name: House Caliburn
records.summary: Usurping ducal house that seized Demeniss in the Blood Coronation.
records.body: [[character:gabriel-caliburn]] took Demeniss by massacring Thorel loyalists in the Blood Coronation and now sits as duke at [[place:demeniss-castle]]. The house wants that seizure made permanent, with Bastier's inquisitors as the whip. Kliff fights Caliburn in story set-pieces, including [[quest:the-blood-coronation]] and later [[quest:a-shadow-in-the-void]]; the house is still not marked hostile-on-sight on the core faction lists, so hostile stays false. Sources disagree whether the reputation board tracks Caliburn as its own row or folds him into Bastier's bucket; that uncertainty is assumed from the missing list row.

reputation.notes: Ranks run War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Story fights against Caliburn move whatever track the game uses for this house. Whether Alliance is even offered is unclear; the core lists never gave Caliburn its own reputation row.

records.name: House Azerian
records.summary: Count's house in Demeniss that opposes Caliburn and raised Damiane.
records.body: [[character:beatrice-azerian]] holds [[place:azerian-manor]] and is one of the nobles who would not bow to Caliburn or Bastier. The house wants the inquisitors off Demeniss; it also raised [[character:damiane]] after House Spencer fell. Kliff and Damiane return to that manor and then hunt Beatrice under the city. [[quest:blazing-fire]], [[quest:clue]] and [[quest:a-fleeting-dream]] are the story beats; Beatrice's death there is permanent.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. The manor infiltration and Damiane's Demeniss work raise this house. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted manor rooms and allied help among Azerian people.

records.name: House Byron
records.summary: Count's house that runs the Eyes of Demeniss and backs Caliburn.
records.body: [[character:count-byron]] (George Byron) keeps an intelligence net from [[place:windmere-manor]] and is written as the Eyes of Demeniss. The house wants Caliburn's mail and foreign business handled in the dark. Kliff is sent into that manor to kill the count during [[quest:bloodied-invitation]]. It is a core Demeniss house, not a roadside bandit camp.

reputation.notes: Standing runs War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. The Windmere job and other court intrigue raise this house. Alliance unlocks exclusive vendors, restricted correspondence rooms and allied help among Byron agents.

records.name: House Marshell
records.summary: Countess's house that funds Bastier as Demeniss's Black Strongbox.
records.body: [[character:ada-marshell]] holds [[place:sungrove-manor]] and pays Bastier's bills; the lists call the house the Black Strongbox. It wants Demeniss politics bent by coin, and it sits against Azerian and Wells. Kliff crosses Sungrove country during the Demeniss chapter. No dedicated Marshell quest record exists here yet; the house is still a core roster row.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Court jobs that touch Marshell money raise standing. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted ledgers and allied help at Sungrove.

records.name: House Wells
records.summary: Southern ducal house sworn to Thorel and openly opposed to Caliburn.
records.body: [[character:drake-wells]] is duke in southern Demeniss and keeps an openly military house sworn to [[faction:house-thorel]]. They want Caliburn and Bastier off the map, and they fight for it in the field. Kliff meets Wells ground during the Chapter 8 suppression work, including [[quest:the-cursed-knight]]. Headquarters is omitted because Thornbriar Fortress has no place record yet.

reputation.notes: Standing runs War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Defending Wells country and finishing the Fortain fight raise this house. Alliance unlocks exclusive vendors, restricted fort rooms and allied troops in the south.

records.name: House Elemore
records.summary: Wealthy Demeniss house, long friends with Azerian, that later turns on the inquisitors.
records.body: [[character:arthur-elemore]] heads a rich, well-placed house that has stood with Azerian for a long time. They want to keep that friendship and their own skin; Bastier's pressure makes them waver, then the Lunar Judgment chain has them move against the inquisitors. Kliff meets that turn as faction work rather than a main-story siege. Headquarters is omitted because Brookfield Manor has no place record yet, and Lunar Judgment has no quest record here.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. The later anti-inquisitor chain is the standing hook the lists give. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted manor rooms and allied help among Elemore people.

records.name: Tariv Sorcerers
records.summary: Village order at Tariv that gives magical protection and keeps a Guardian Tree rite.
records.body: The sorcerers of [[place:tariv]] give magical guidance and protection and hold a Guardian Tree coming-of-age for their youths. They want that rite and that village kept. Kliff meets Tariv as a Demeniss-listed settlement sitting near the desert edge. No source read here names a head sorcerer.

records.name: Bastier's Inquisitors
records.summary: Caliburn's political persecution force under Grand General Lucian Bastier.
records.body: [[character:bastier]] (Lucian Bastier) runs this persecution arm for Caliburn from Demeniss, and the lists also call them Righteous Inquisitors. They want dissenters broken; the same lists say the office has slid far from whatever purpose it first claimed. Kliff and Damiane meet them through the late Demeniss chapter, and Damiane fights Bastier in [[quest:a-fleeting-dream]]. Headquarters is the capital they enforce, [[place:demeniss-castle]].

records.name: Silvermoon Trade Collective
records.summary: Demeniss merchant collective written as an ethical foil to Goldleaf.
records.body: The collective is a Demeniss trade group that sells itself as cleaner than the profit-only [[faction:goldleaf-merchant-guild]]. It wants honest ledgers and a contrast banner. Kliff can meet its merchants as civilian trade, not as a siege. The row is Game8-only in the research file, and no leader or hall is named.

reputation.notes: Standing runs War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Fair-trade jobs in Demeniss raise this collective. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted warehouses and allied help at its posts.

records.name: Marni
records.summary: Marni's own circle, driving a technological-utopia project for Delesyia.
records.body: Game8 lists this banner under the name Marni, separate from the wider Society of Progress even though [[character:marni]] leads both. The circle wants Delesyia remade as a machine city from [[place:marnis-laboratorium]]. Kliff meets Marni as a living person in that city and again at the castle gate in the epilogue. [[quest:evolving-city]] is the late confirmation of those plans.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Delesyia story work around Marni's shops and plans raises standing. Alliance unlocks exclusive vendors, restricted workshops and allied help in the steel city.

records.name: Society of Progress
records.summary: Broader mechanization movement Marni leads across Delesyia.
records.body: The Society is the wider research-and-build movement around [[character:marni]], listed as its own Game8 row beside the narrower Marni circle. It wants machines in every street of Delesyia. Kliff walks that program through Chapter 11, including the forgotten-land fight that sits on this storyline. [[quest:master-of-a-forgotten-land]] is the named beat; Golden Star is a boss on that path, not a second faction.

reputation.notes: Ranks run War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Society jobs and the Chapter 11 machine-city work raise standing. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted foundries and allied help around Delesyia Castle.

records.name: Delesyia National Institute
records.summary: Official Delesyia school of mechanical engineering, slower than Marni's own work.
records.body: The institute studies machines as a public academy and is written as trailing [[character:marni]]'s private pace. It wants official engineering on the books. Kliff meets it as civic Delesyia texture rather than a raid. No source read here names a director.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Academic errands in the steel city raise standing. Alliance unlocks exclusive vendors, restricted lecture halls and allied help on institute ground.

records.name: Delesyian Aerial Force
records.summary: Delesyia service building airship warfare for a sky-conquest program.
records.body: The Aerial Force develops airship war and is written as a sky-conquest project. It wants the air over Delesyia owned. Kliff visits the aeronautical works during [[quest:fortress-keys]]; tying the headquarters to [[place:aeronautical-research-base]] is assumed from that being the named air-research site. No source read here names a commander.

records.name: Ironflame Orcs
records.summary: Gorthak orc force that forges steel and weapons, led by Valgash.
records.body: [[character:valgash]] leads the Ironflame from [[place:gorthak-ironworks]], written as the strongest force in Gorthak. They want steel and weapons coming off the line. Kliff follows Valgash through Chapter 10 and speaks with him again after Marni's Clockwork Mantis falls. [[quest:master-of-the-ironworks]] is the named visit.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Ironworks jobs and the Chapter 10 smith work raise this tribe. Alliance unlocks exclusive vendors, restricted forges and allied help at Gorthak.

records.name: Ironwheel of Dewhaven
records.summary: Dewhaven workshop guild that builds everyday machines for people, not armies.
records.body: The Ironwheel works from [[place:dewhaven-castle]] and builds ordinary machines meant to help people. It wants that human-first line kept, against Marni's more martial pace. Kliff meets Dewhaven as a workshop town rather than a siege. No source read here names a workshop head.

reputation.notes: Ranks run War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Workshop jobs in Dewhaven raise standing. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted benches and allied help at the castle works.

records.name: Marni's Tinkertons
records.summary: Tech-minded Tinkerton residents who prefer watching the sky to pushing research.
records.body: The Tinkertons are Marni-aligned residents at Tinkerton and Timberton who would rather watch the sky than run the next experiment. They want that slower life kept. Kliff can meet them around [[place:tinkerton-dig-site]]. The row is Game8-only in the research file, and no leader is named.

records.name: Gearmelt Confectionery
records.summary: Delesyia chocolate works whose trade goods draw bandits.
records.body: Gearmelt mass-makes chocolate in Delesyia and sells it as a popular trade good. It wants those shipments through, and bandits want the same crates. Kliff can meet the confectionery as civilian trade and as escort work. The row is Game8-only in the research file; no leader or shop hall is named, so those fields are omitted.

reputation.notes: Standing runs War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Escorting chocolate and finishing confectionery requests raise this guild. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted kitchens and allied help at its works.

records.name: Redfox Merchants
records.summary: Delesyia trade brokers who move regional goods from a named trading post.
records.body: The Redfox Merchants handle resource distribution across Delesyia from a trading post named for them. They want goods moving, not a private army. Kliff meets them as regional brokers. Headquarters is omitted because the Redfox Merchant Trading Post has no place record yet.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Brokerage jobs and cargo work raise this guild. Alliance unlocks exclusive vendors, restricted depots and allied help at the post.

records.name: Cogknights
records.summary: Delesyia militia that fields Marni's machines as war engines.
records.body: The Cogknights are a tactical militia that rolls Marni's machines into the field. They want those engines ready, not sitting in a museum. Kliff meets them as Delesyia's armed civic arm. No source read here names a captain.

records.name: Wyvernflames
records.summary: Foreign wyvern-riders who massacre and enslave from Windridge Fortress.
records.body: The Wyvernflames are foreign riders who take slaves and burn locals, holding Windridge Fortress. They want Delesyia ground under their saddles. Kliff meets them as hostile occupiers. Headquarters is omitted because Windridge Fortress has no place record yet.

records.name: Arcosa Tribe
records.summary: Desert tribe that holds Arcosa, written as the region's most prosperous village.
records.body: The Arcosa Tribe keeps the walled town of [[place:arcosa]] and its four watchtowers. They want that prosperity defended against desert raids. Kliff meets the town as a desert hub rather than a hostile camp. No source read here names a tribal chief.

records.name: Muiquun Outlaws
records.summary: Exile refuge at Muiquun where staying alive, not a written code, decides who lasts.
records.body: The outlaws hold [[place:muiquun]] as a place for the exiled, and the lists say nothing but the will to stay alive counts as law there. They want that refuge left standing. Kliff can walk the village without it being marked as an on-sight raid; the research file marks hostility as depends, so hostile stays false. No source read here names a boss of the refuge.

records.name: Lords of Unclaimed Lands
records.summary: Independent desert dwellers who answer to no duchy or guild.
records.body: The Lords of Unclaimed Lands are ungoverned desert people, not a noble house despite the name. They want no duke and no guild charter. Kliff meets them as scattered desert civilians. No source read here names a speaker or a seat, so those fields are omitted.

records.name: Redwind Merchant Guild
records.summary: Desert guild that trades exotic goods and rare treasures along the Saltroad.
records.body: Redwind moves strange goods and rare finds across the Crimson Desert by the Saltroad. It wants those caravans paid and intact. Kliff meets the guild as desert trade rather than a siege. No source read here names a trademaster or a hall, so those fields are omitted.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Saltroad escorts and exotic-goods jobs raise this guild. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted caravan stores and allied help on the road.

records.name: Sage of the Desert
records.summary: Itinerant goblin preacher whose harsh lessons are meant to wake pilgrims.
records.body: The Sage of the Desert is both a banner and the goblin preacher who walks it. The teaching is written as a harsh awakening, not a gentle homily. Kliff meets that road during Chapter 9. [[quest:the-sage-of-the-desert]] is the named beat; there is no fixed hall, so headquarters is omitted.

records.name: Sandfang Marauders
records.summary: Goblin wolf-riders trying to unify the desert under bandit rule.
records.body: The Sandfang are goblin-led wolf-riders with the widest bandit country in the Crimson Desert. They want that waste under one outlaw banner. Kliff meets them as hostile desert camps. No source read here names a captain.

records.name: Goldenscale Bandits
records.summary: Dwarf-led iguana riders, dismissed by rivals as petty thieves.
records.body: The Goldenscale ride iguanas and are written as a dwarf-led desert crew. They want easy plunder; other bands treat them as small-time. Kliff meets them as hostile desert fights. No source read here names a leader.

records.name: Dusksong
records.summary: Deserter-soldier bandits in the Crimson Desert who fight with stolen weapons.
records.body: Dusksong is a deserter crew that kept its army kit and turned it on the road. They want that stolen steel to pay. Kliff meets them as hostile desert bandits, separate from the Bursada research team that shares a Game8 heading. No source read here names a captain.

records.name: Savage Fangs
records.summary: Nomadic boar-riding raiders under Ravok, mostly ex-Kharonso trolls in the wetlands.
records.body: [[character:ravok]] formed this raiding band after leaving Kharonso's rigid customs, and most of the riders are trolls from that village. They want travelers' packs, not a new town. Lists place their ground in both Pailune wetlands and the Crimson Desert; this record keeps the desert region the task asked for. The row is a single gaming.tools snippet, so the wetland seat and the Kharonso origin are assumed.

records.name: The Faceless
records.summary: Masked desert bandits who call their plunder liberation and keep to themselves.
records.body: The Faceless wear masks and sell their raids as liberation while staying self-reliant. They want that story believed and their caches unshared. Kliff meets them as hostile desert crews. No source read here names a leader.

records.name: The Helms
records.summary: Vicious desert tribe that builds war machines from stolen technology.
records.body: The Helms are written as the most vicious desert tribe and they bolt stolen machines into war gear. They want conquest, not a market stall. Kliff meets them as hostile desert fighters. No source read here names a chief.

records.name: Twilight Messengers
records.summary: Freesword company under Merrick that tolls desert guilds and now takes Demeniss coin.
records.body: [[character:merrick]], called the Knight of Fortune, leads a freesword company that answers only to pay. They toll merchant guilds crossing the desert and are currently taking orders from Demeniss. Kliff meets them as hostile desert mercenaries holding named ground such as Dawnreach and the Timeworn Ruins. Headquarters is omitted because Crimson Mountains Fortress has no place record yet; the row is snippet-only.

records.name: Bursada Ruins Research Team
records.summary: Rainforest artifact team that bandits hunt for the treasure it studies.
records.body: The Bursada team works the rainforest for artifacts and is written as a research crew, not a second Dusksong. They want the ruins read before bandits strip them. Kliff can meet them as civilian scholars under threat. The row is Game8-only in the research file; no leader or named camp record exists, so those fields are omitted.

reputation.notes: Standing runs War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Guarding the team and finishing rainforest study jobs raise standing. Alliance opens exclusive vendors, restricted digs and allied help at the ruins.

records.name: Giant Yard's Research Group
records.summary: Desert ecology team studying a mysterious red tree in Giant's Yard.
records.body: This group studies desert ecology and is written as chasing a strange red tree. They want that tree understood, not cut for coin. Kliff can meet them as field scholars in Giant's Yard country. The row is Game8-only in the research file; no leader is named, and the nearby resource camp is not confirmed as their hall, so headquarters is omitted.

reputation.notes: The five ranks are War, Hostile, Neutral, Friendly and Alliance. Ecology jobs around Giant's Yard raise standing. Alliance unlocks exclusive vendors, restricted study plots and allied help at the tree.

records.name: Whitesand Retreat
records.summary: Varnia debate hall open only to high-ranking Atima believers.
records.body: The Whitesand Retreat is a philosophical hall in Varnia for high-ranking Atima believers only. It wants that debate kept inside the faith's upper ranks. Kliff can meet it as a closed religious room, not a raid. The row is Game8-only in the research file; Varnia has no place record yet, so headquarters is omitted.
